title: Do Generate–Verify–Repair Guards Improve LLM NetOps Outputs? A Paired Emulator Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n=200 natural-language NetOps intents; study_id cnd-001-5f3a) to evaluate whether a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline that applies a deterministic verifier and a deterministic rule-based repair operator to a single shared LLM candidate improves emulator-executable success versus ungated LLM output. Generation used gpt-5-mini; the guarded arm invoked a deterministic three-stage validator and a deterministic repair operator with repair_budget ≤1 (no extra LLM calls). Artifact-backed primary outcomes: baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded = 200/200 (1.000); paired contingency n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact binomial on discordant pairs) yields p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target is excluded by the observed CI because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. We describe the deterministic validator and repair operator, provide auditable exemplar diagnostics for the single repaired episode, report an aggregate difficulty-label breakdown for the confirmatory bank (artifact-cited), and discuss operational implications and limitations. All prompts, provider traces, validator/repair traces, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle.

sections.introduction:
Automating routine network operations (NetOps) changes with large language models (LLMs) promises reduced manual effort but raises operational-safety and correctness questions: will LLM-produced configuration artifacts execute correctly when applied to control planes? Prior work documents intent-to-configuration prototypes, structured-output failure modes (missing commands, misordering, protected-field modification), and mitigation proposals such as retrieval-augmentation, constrained decoding, verifier-assisted repair, and multi-stage tool augmentation. However, there is limited execution-grounded evidence quantifying the marginal benefit of applying a bounded deterministic repair to the same initial LLM candidate under realistic provider-call budgets.

To address this gap we implemented and preregistered a paired, shared-initial-generation design (study_id cnd-001-5f3a) that conserves hosted-model calls by sharing a single initial candidate across both arms: (A) baseline = accept initial candidate; (B) guarded = apply deterministic validator and, if uniquely repairable, a deterministic rule-based repair operator (repair_budget ≤1). This shared-candidate estimand is operationally relevant when hosted-model calls are constrained (e.g., cost or audit concerns). Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation under the shared-candidate estimand; (2) concise, auditable descriptions of the deterministic three-stage validator and the deterministic repair operator used in the guarded pipeline; (3) representative exemplar traces and an aggregate difficulty-label summary for the confirmatory bank; and (4) exact-test justification and interpretation appropriate for small discordant counts, including a clear statement of why the preregistered power target was not achievable given the realized baseline.
sections.related_work: Work on LLMs for NetOps splits into three strands relevant to our study. First, intent-to-configuration efforts show that LLMs can produce CLI-like sequences from natural-language intents but often emit structurally or semantically invalid outputs without additional constraints; empirical intent-translation prototypes and surveys document such failure modes and prototype success under curated conditions (Nguyen et al., 2024) [doi:10.1002/nem.2313]. Second, mitigation work across domains has proposed RAG (retrieval-augmented generation), live schema grounding, constrained/grammar-aware decoding, and verifier-assisted repair; these techniques reduce but do not fully eliminate hallucinations and require careful domain adaptation for device-specific CLI dialects (Geng et al., 2023; Wołk, 2025). Third, formal deterministic verification tools (NetKAT variants, ensemble verifiers) and emulator-backed validators can check reachability, isolation, and many workflow properties; they are natural assurance layers for generated configurations (Suárez Acevedo et al., 2026) [doi:10.1145/3808318]. Generate–verify–repair architectures are often proposed as pragmatic patterns, but fully instrumented, execution-grounded, preregistered paired measurements under constrained call budgets have been scarce; our study targets that precise gap (G2 in our evidence synthesis).
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and experimental plan: We preregistered a paired, shared-initial-generation confirmatory protocol (study_id cnd-001-5f3a). For each of n = 200 curated natural-language intents the hosted model produced one shared initial candidate. Baseline accepts that candidate verbatim; guarded runs the deterministic validator and, if the violation family is in a preregistered repairable set with a unique deterministic mapping, applies a deterministic repair (repair_budget ≤1). The primary estimand is the paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline); the preregistered primary test is the exact two-sided McNemar implemented as an exact-binomial test on discordant pairs. Planned maximum hosted-model calls = 400; realized model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; deterministic repair-stage calls = 1). The execution environment used Dockerized Mininet+FRR and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the canonical validator. The preregistration, task generator, and all artifacts are archived (preregistration SHA-256: e5c5fdbd...; execution raw results SHA-256: e3bb0089...).

Task bank and scoring rules: The confirmatory bank contains 200 intent–expected-configuration pairs generated deterministically. Each task payload records initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence (authoritative per-task commands), workflow_policies (e.g., make-before-break, protected interfaces), and difficulty metadata. The scoring rule (full_intent_constraint_validation) requires that generated configurations (a) parse syntactically into canonical CLI-like statements, (b) include the task’s required_sequence (presence and order), (c) respect dependency and group-activity policies, (d) preserve protected-interface values, and (e) produce an emulator-observed final_state equal to expected_final_state when applied to the deterministic emulator. Provider/API generation failures were treated per the preregistered missingness plan as arm failures; none occurred in the confirmatory run.

Deterministic validator: The validator deterministically executes three ordered stages and emits a machine-readable trace used by scoring and repair logic. Stage 1 — syntactic parsing and canonical normalization: tokenizes CLI-like lines and produces normalized_configuration; fatal syntax errors (SYNTAX_PARSE_ERROR) block repair. Stage 2 — structural/workflow checks: deterministically verifies presence and ordering of required_sequence and enforces dependency/group policies, emitting deterministic violation codes (e.g., MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND, DEPENDENCY_VIOLATION, PROTECTED_INTERFACE_MODIFICATION). Stage 3 — deterministic emulator application: the normalized_configuration is applied to the emulator, producing observed final_state; validation_after.valid is true iff observed final_state equals expected_final_state. Each episode's validator_trace (parsed_command_count, normalized_configuration, violation_codes, validation_before/after) is archived for audit.

Deterministic repair operator: The preregistered repair operator is a deterministic, rule-based transformer invoked only when violation_count > 0 and the violation family belongs to a preregistered repairable set whose mapping to a deterministic transformation is unique. Repairs are computed wholly from the task manifest (no extra LLM calls) and are bounded: at most one deterministic repair attempt per episode in the confirmatory run. The operator implements three canonical deterministic transformations: (1) Insertion — insert missing required commands at canonical positions derived from required_sequence; (2) Reordering — stable minimal block moves to resolve dependency violations while preserving intra-block token order; (3) Preservation enforcement — replace offending modifications to protected fields with canonical values from initial_state or expected_final_state. If multiple equally plausible deterministic repairs exist, the operator abstains (no change) and the episode remains a guarded failure; such abstentions are flagged in the repair_trace and counted as nonrepairable. All repair traces are archived.
sections.results:
Execution summary and primary outcomes: The confirmatory run completed all planned episodes (400 episodes = 200 paired intents) with no provider/API failures. Condition-level counts (artifact-backed analysis/condition_summary.csv) show baseline_successes = 199/200 (0.995) and guarded_successes = 200/200 (1.000). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005.

Exact-test and CI: The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact-binomial on discordant pairs) uses n = n10 + n01 discordants. Observed discordants n = 1 (n10 = 1, n01 = 0), yielding an exact two-sided p-value p = 1.0 (artifact-backed; analysis/results.json). Complementary uncertainty quantification used a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) producing 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015]. Because the preregistered primary-effect target was an absolute 0.15 improvement, the observed CI excludes that magnitude under the shared-candidate estimand: the realized near-ceiling baseline compresses discordant counts and reduces sensitivity to large absolute effects under this design.

Aggregate difficulty-label distribution (artifact-cited): To contextualize task difficulty we report the aggregated counts of per-task difficulty labels extracted from the archived task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; SHA-256: eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a). The confirmatory bank labels are distributed as: easy = 8, medium = 64, hard = 88, very_hard = 40 (total = 200). These counts are recorded verbatim in execution/task_manifest.jsonl and enable readers to assess the curated bank’s challenge profile; the full manifest is archived for audit and re-analysis.

Single repaired episode — auditable exemplar: The deterministic validator reported validation_before.valid == false for exactly one episode (pair_id = pair-00137; task_id = task-00137) and the repair operator was invoked once (deterministic repair invocations = 1). The validator emitted violation_codes = ["MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND"] for that episode. The preregistered repair rule applied was Insertion: the operator deterministically inserted the missing required_sequence command at the canonical index derived from the task manifest, converting the normalized_configuration from the pre-repair snippet (execution/raw_results.jsonl entry for task-00137, shared_initial_candidate SHA-256: 9a3f...; normalized pre-repair excerpt: "interface svc1 admin down\ninterface svc1 vlan 42\n") to the post-repair normalized_configuration archived in the repair trace (execution/repairs/task-00137-repair.json SHA-256: 4b2c...; post-repair excerpt: "interface svc1 admin down\ninterface svc1 vlan 42\ninterface svc1 admin up\n"). The repair trace documents the unique mapping decision (missing required_sequence entry present in task manifest) and the canonical insertion index; these per-episode artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256: e3bb0089... and the repair-trace path above) for inspection. The single deterministic repair converted that episode into a validator-passing final configuration, producing the sole guarded-only success (n10 = 1).

Repair diagnostics and provider accounting: Provider-call accounting (deterministic_reconciliation.json) records hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, cache_miss_count = 201, stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1}. Syntactic/parse failures = 0 and no API errors occurred. All per-episode validator and repair traces are archived (execution/*) to permit post-hoc failure taxonomy analysis.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation: Under the shared-initial-generation estimand and this curated confirmatory distribution the ungated gpt-5-mini generator produced near-perfect candidates (199/200). Deterministic validators create structured violation codes that enable targeted deterministic repairs; in a low-error regime the marginal yield of a conservative rule-based repair on the same candidate is small but auditable and low-cost. For operators constrained by hosted-call budgets, the guarded shared-candidate design preserves low model-call cost while providing an assurance gate; when maximizing per-intent pass rates is paramount, independent-resampling or LLM-invoked iterative repair (at higher provider cost) are alternatives.

Statistical sensitivity and preregistered power violation: The preregistered power analysis targeted an absolute effect of 0.15 assuming a baseline ≈0.5 and n = 200. The observed baseline (0.995) dramatically reduces expected discordant-pair counts and hence power for detecting the preregistered effect under the shared-candidate estimand; concretely, only one discordant pair was observed (n = 1), precluding rejection of the null for two-sided tests even though the guarded arm corrected a single auditable case. This outcome is not a methodological error but reflects the interaction of the paired shared-candidate design with a near-ceiling baseline—the confirmatory test and the paired-bootstrap CI correctly quantify the resulting uncertainty (see analysis/results.json and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). Future confirmatory designs that seek greater sensitivity to modest absolute gains should consider independent-resampling estimands or intentionally sampling higher-difficulty or adversarial intents to increase discordant opportunities.

Design trade-offs and practitioner guidance: The run’s accounting (model_calls_used = 201; repair invocations = 1) quantifies the low marginal provider cost of the guarded shared-candidate approach. Deterministic repairs that operate from authoritative task manifests produce auditable, low-churn edits; when operational constraints require minimal hosted-model usage and maximal auditability, the shared-candidate guarded design is attractive. Where operator policy permits additional calls, independent-resampling or LLM-guided repair loops may raise aggregate pass rates but at higher cost and more complex evidentiary traces to audit. Deterministic validators are recommended as a mandatory assurance layer when auditable, repeatable checks and low-latency failure explanations are required.

Threats to validity: Internal validity is strong for the paired estimand and deterministic scoring; construct validity depends on emulator fidelity—our deterministic emulator models control-plane state deterministically but cannot fully capture runtime effects such as BGP convergence timing or device firmware idiosyncrasies. External validity is limited by a single LLM (gpt-5-mini) and a curated synthetic bank focused on small device changes; generalization to multivendor CLI diversity, real-device idiosyncrasies, or adversarial intents is limited. Conclusion validity is constrained by the near-ceiling baseline that produced only one discordant pair; exact McNemar is appropriate for small discordant counts but the study’s sensitivity to detect large absolute effects under the preregistered assumptions was compromised. These constraints shape the practical takeaway: deterministic validators provide auditable assurance and low-cost marginal yield in low-error regimes, but different estimands, broader banks, or additional repair budgets are needed to evaluate larger end-to-end gains.
sections.conclusion: We executed an autonomy-locked, preregistered paired experiment to measure whether a bounded generate–verify–repair guard improves emulator-executable success for LLM-generated NetOps configurations under a shared-candidate generation budget. Ungated gpt-5-mini succeeded in 199/200 confirmatory cases; the deterministic guarded pipeline succeeded in 200/200. The observed paired difference = 0.005 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.015]) does not support the preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target because the baseline was near-ceiling. Deterministic repair-on-the-same-candidate yielded a single auditable correction in this curated bank; deterministic validators remain valuable, auditable assurance gates for operational NetOps pipelines. All prompts, responses, validator traces, the single repair trace, analysis code, and the preregistration are archived for independent audit and re-analysis (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256: e3bb0089..., execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256: eb2f045f8a62...).

disclosure_statement:
Disclosure: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock defined by the initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human involvement prior to the lock was limited to selecting the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approving the master prompt. No manual human editing of technical content, figures, captions, references, results, or manuscript text occurred after the lock. The autonomous pipeline performed literature search and verification, research-gap selection, preregistration (study_id cnd-001-5f3a), code generation, experiment execution, artifact capture, deterministic analysis, internal critique, peer-review checks, and manuscript drafting.

Models and tooling: Generation requested gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version in execution/model_configuration.json; execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256: a40e96e2...). Validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing syntactic parsing, structural/workflow checks, and deterministic emulator application. Repairs in the confirmatory run were applied by deterministic code only (no additional LLM calls). The execution environment used Dockerized Mininet+FRR images orchestrated by adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistered and enforced settings (not altered post-lock) include: primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample = n=200 paired intents; maximum model-call budget = 400; repair budget ≤1 deterministic repair iteration; primary analysis = exact McNemar two-sided (exact-binomial on discordant pairs); bootstrap CIs = 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729. Execution accounting (artifact-backed): the run completed 400 episodes with model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; repair-stage calls = 1). All prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, repair traces (the single invoked repair trace), analysis artifacts, and the execution manifest are archived in the study evidence bundle (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256: e3bb0089..., execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256: eb2f045f8a62...).
limitations: Synthetic, curated confirmatory task bank focused on small single- and small multi-device changes; not comprehensive of production NetOps workloads (multivendor CLI dialects, hardware idiosyncrasies, dynamic control-plane timing).
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) evaluated; findings do not imply multi-model generality.
Deterministic emulator + validator model control-plane behavior but cannot fully capture real-world runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or vendor-specific runtime effects.
Preregistered repair budget limited to a single deterministic repair iteration; different repair strategies or additional iterations might yield different outcomes.
Shared-initial-generation design reduces model-call cost and isolates repair-on-same-candidate effectiveness but reduces external generalizability compared with independent-resampling estimands.
Near-ceiling baseline success limited statistical power to analyze failure-mode distributions in the confirmatory set; exploratory failure-taxonomy conclusions are therefore constrained.
Adversarial or out-of-distribution intents (e.g., jailbreaks, malformed ambiguous intents) were not included in the confirmatory set and require separate evaluation.

Full per-task difficulty label counts for all 200 confirmatory intents are recorded in execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256: eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a) in the archived evidence bundle; the manuscript includes an aggregate summary of those counts for contextualization.
